claims.text: A page exists at /docs/support/provider-support-policy/ (the Provider support policy page in Pulumi docs).
The Pulumi provider support policy page describes how long Pulumi maintains each provider major version.
Some Pulumi providers receive long-term security updates, and the provider support policy page identifies which providers get them.
Pulumi focuses on actively supporting the latest released major version of the providers it maintains.
For a set of widely used providers, Pulumi ships security updates for the previous major version for up to a year, or until the next major version is released, whichever comes first.
The provider support policy page at /docs/support/provider-support-policy/ lists the covered providers and what a long-term support release contains.
Older major versions of Pulumi-maintained providers receive no patches at all.
The Pulumi Registry shows the current version for all providers maintained by Pulumi.
A page exists at /docs/support/provider-support-policy/ titled Provider support policy.
Pulumi does not automatically roll back changes during an update if an error occurs; it completes pending operations in progress then exits and reports the error.
Pulumi Cloud provides built-in drift detection, and `pulumi up --refresh` refreshes and applies in a single step.
Experimental features in Pulumi are always opt-in and can change or be removed without a deprecation cycle; PULUMI_EXPERIMENTAL=true enables them.
Pulumi actively maintains the latest released major version of every provider it publishes.
For a set of widely used providers, Pulumi ships security updates for the previous major version for up to 12 months, or until the next major version is released, whichever comes first.
The providers receiving long-term support are AWS, Azure Classic, Azure Native, Azure AD, Command, Docker Build, GCP, Kubernetes, TLS, and Vault.
Registry pages exist at /registry/packages/ for aws, azure, azure-native, azuread, command, docker-build, gcp, kubernetes, tls, and vault.

The LTS branch ships High/Critical CVE security patches, including fixes for CVEs in the provider's code or direct dependencies and fixes for broken internal infrastructure on the LTS branch needed to ship them.
An LTS release does not contain new upstream API versions, new resources or properties, performance improvements, non-security bug fixes, or compatibility with newer language runtime versions.
LTS providers remain compatible with the Pulumi version they were frozen at unless security fixes require otherwise.
Exactly one long-term support major exists per covered provider at any time.
When N+1 ships, N becomes the new LTS major and the old LTS major reaches end of life the same day, regardless of remaining 12-month window.
Within the LTS major, only the latest minor version receives patches; earlier minors are frozen.
LTS releases are available through the same standard package registries as current-major releases but are tagged differently.
Customers pinning to a specific major version automatically receive patch releases as they ship, and pinning is recommended.
Older majors than the LTS version receive no patches; if v3 is newest, v2 is N-1 and v1 and earlier are end of life.
The current major (N) receives new features, resources, bug fixes, security patches, dependency upgrades, and new upstream API versions until N+1 ships.
LTS (N-1) lasts up to 12 months from N's release or until N+1 ships, and ships security updates in the provider's code or direct dependencies.
Versions N-2 and older are end of life and receive no updates.
